name: Zielinski Cup: First Round

date.source: The broadcast's own eight posted parts, all dated 30 December 1997.

matches.note: Ronnie D. knocked out the referee, hit the Evangelist with his own NeCW title belt, and pinned him; a second official ruled the cover illegal and let the match continue, but Ronnie D. went on to win it outright with a DDT off the belt at 14:29.

John "Fucked Up Brain" Smith ran in and chaired Rune from the apron, letting Harley Robinson pin him; Smith then turned on Robinson too, brainbustering him and raising Rune's hand, and the two left together after trashing Robinson's motorcycle.
Sean Waltman won at 14:35 with a top-rope brain buster; Moo Kame attacked him from behind after the bell with a facelock DDT.
Vampyro pinned Wardancer at 15:54 with his feet on the bottom rope after a 450 splash; the commentary called the finish a cheat.

Alex Extreme had disguised himself as the match's own substitute referee; he low-blowed Samael, revealed himself, hit his own DDT finisher, and a second referee ran in to count the pin in three seconds.
Jinsei Shakanuzi won at 11:23 with his Capoeira Dance finisher, a springboard somersault legdrop off a reversed Michinoku Driver.
John "Fucked Up Brain" Smith rolled Joe Mama up for the pin after a long match; both men had traded cheating attempts throughout.

"Top Dog" Rick Styles won at 12:23, accompanied to the ring by his manager Mark R. Rose; the broadcast team accused both Styles and the earlier winner Harley Robinson of cheating their way through the round.

appearances.note: Accompanied Rick Styles to the ring for the main event.
Called the tournament's first round from ringside, as one of the Cup's two organizers.
Co-called the broadcast for most of the card, stepping away for one match.
Introduced every wrestler and announced every match result.

evidence.note: The tournament's own first-round broadcast script.

notes: The Zielinski Cup was announced 12 November 1997 by the AeWF's own two co-founders as four planned tournaments (singles and tag brackets each for AeWF wrestlers and for newsgroup entrants); the bracket drawn on air 29 November 1997 narrowed this to one 16-entrant singles bracket, plus a separate four-team tag elimination (the Specialists, XXX, General Punishment, and the reigning AeWF tag champions the Maniacs) for a "Special Zielinski Tag Team Cup," whose result does not survive in the held record. Three of the eight drawn first-round pairings changed by fight night: Brian Fury vs. Jinsei Shakanuzi became Jinsei Shakanuzi vs. Mr. Excellence, Alex Extreme vs. General Punishment became Alex Extreme vs. Samael, and Zoto vs. Rick Styles became Professor Payne vs. Rick Styles; no surviving document explains the changes. The Cup's singles final was scheduled for 23 January 1998 and its tag final for 9 March 1998, both outside the held record's 1997 holdings; no further round of either bracket is structured here.

name: Vicious Circle Tonight

date.source: The broadcast's own subject line dates the card 27 November 1997; posted to the newsgroup the following day in five parts, of which four survive in the held record (part one is not held — an honest gap).

matches.note: Ruled a double disqualification after Sean Waltman's manager and wife Inga Waltman chaired Floyd Malloy; Joe Mama then entered the ring, grabbed Inga Waltman, and had to be talked down by Malloy.
Joe Mama no-sold his own title defense as a joke, taking a fake leg cramp and letting Samael pin him for the belt.

Ordered by the promotion's own on-screen management to defend the title in a real fight after the King of Extreme Crown farce, Joe Mama chose Mon-STARR as his opponent and again threw the match, taking one punch and staying down for the count.

The Evangelist escaped a power-move beatdown with a low blow and won the vacated-in-spirit title by sleeper hold, aided by his own choir forming a human wall against the ringside Vicious Circle stable.

appearances.note: Interfered with a steel chair on her husband's behalf, then was taken hostage in the ring by Joe Mama before Floyd Malloy talked him down.
Joined the broadcast table as Joe Mama's brother and a guest color commentator.
Called the broadcast throughout, including Joe Mama's own "Mama Said" interview segment.
Entered the ring with President Zielinski to sanction Joe Mama's title defense and order a real match for the Television Championship.
Confronted Joe Mama over his staged King of Extreme Crown defense and ordered a genuine Television Championship match in its place.

evidence.source: rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy, 27–28 November 1997 (parts two through five of five; part one not held)
evidence.note: The promotion's own weekly broadcast script.

notes: Joe Mama enters this broadcast already billed, in the commentary's own words, as "the first AEWF superstar to have held all the singles belts, except the King of the Air"; he leaves it having lost both the King of Extreme Crown and the Television Championship in the same night, the latter changing hands twice before the night is out. His own résumé credit as an "ex-ICWF Tag Team champion," raised elsewhere in this collection's own Zielinski Cup coverage, matches no roster on file for any of this collection's three documented ICWF entities and stays unassignable; a stablemate's own aside this same night, accusing the promotion's management of "slapping every wrestler in the ICWF in the face," suggests "ICWF" may also have been used here as an in-story stable name inside the Vicious Circle rather than as any of those outside federations, but no further document confirms it.
